verdict.rationale: GlitchTip has no first-party SDKs of its own. Its documented approach is compatibility with Sentry's open-source client SDKs, and it publishes setup instructions for any Sentry-compatible SDK. Community users confirm this works reliably, so developers can build against a documented, supported SDK ecosystem, but it is borrowed rather than GlitchTip-owned. Missing for 10: first-party GlitchTip-branded SDKs, SDKs for its management API (no OpenAPI spec was found), and per-language SDK reference docs maintained by GlitchTip.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can build against official SDKs

citations.quote: GlitchTip can use Sentry's open source SDKs to receive error data from your application.
See our general SDK setup instructions for getting started with any Sentry-compatible SDK.
Our app is compatible with Sentry client SDKs, but easier to run.
